html:
SMTO-SKL-0113 — The Slack sign-in took too long and expired

GUID: 779eb0df-8279-5f86-a28c-887511daabf3
Slug: slack-oauth-timeout
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: slack

What happened

  • Each Slack sign-in link lasts 10 minutes, and this one ran out before Slack sent you back. No Slack workspace was connected, and the link can't be used again.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Before you start, sign in to Slack in your browser and have any approval you need from your Slack workspace ready. Being ready means you can finish Slack's page well before the 10 minutes run out.
  2. Ask SMTO to connect Slack again and open the new link right away. Don't use the old one. The expired link can never work again; only a new one starts a fresh 10 minutes.
  3. Approve the permissions on Slack's page without leaving it, and don't restart SMTO meanwhile. A restart cancels every unfinished sign-in.

What success looks like

  • The Slack sign-in tab shows a message starting with "Connected" that says you can close the window.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send it to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep requesting new links without finishing them; unfinished links pile up and can block new ones.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Slack OAuth callback matched a pending authorization whose 10-minute lifetime had already passed, so the shared browser flow reported authorization_timeout and did not exchange the code.

What this means

  • Shared browser OAuth finds that the matched pending authorization transaction has expired. The diagnostic performs no Slack request. Inspect the original receipt and operation stage to determine effects; keep workspace, principal and exact channel/message identities fixed during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Shared browser OAuth finds that the matched pending authorization transaction has expired.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the original flow's expiration and discard its consumed state.

How to fix it

  • BrowserOAuth.finish consumed the matching state but found it expired (600-second lifetime); SlackOAuth.error maps authorization_timeout to oauth_timeout. Start a new slack.connect and complete consent within ten minutes on the same Server process.
  • Restart slack.connect and complete consent within ten minutes.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect exact provider state and authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • A fresh flow completes within the ten-minute lifetime.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • The diagnostic performs no Slack request. Inspect the original receipt and operation stage to determine effects; keep workspace, principal and exact channel/message identities fixed during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
